5.text: GREEK ORTHODOX MISSION. — The Russian Orthodox Church has always
5.note: Run-in second-level heading, printed in small capitals; keyed as plain ASCII capitals per keying_spec.md §2.13.

6.text: been merely a branch of the Russian Government. Its missionary work in

7.text: Siberia was performed solely at the expense of the State and under the control

8.text: of the Administration. One of the influential participants in this work even

9.text: goes so far as to say, “Most of all, they [the natives] point to the fact that

10.text: there does not exist a direct order of the Czar for the adoption of the Russian

11.text: creed. They say, ‘If the Czar should desire that all of us become Russians,

12.text: he would certainly send an order to that effect.’ They understand by instinct

13.text: that the adoption of the Russian Creed is not only an affair of the Church,

14.text: but also that of the State.”¹ On the other hand, and in direct connection

15.text: with this position, the history of the activity of Greek-Orthodox missionaries

16.text: among the tribes of Siberia, as Mr. Waldemar Jochelson justly remarks,² cannot

17.text: be considered honorable, with the exception of a few noble personalities, like

18.text: the Aleut missionary Veniaminov or the Altai missionary Verbitzky.

19.text: The first attempt to baptize the Chukchee was probably made immediately

20.text: after the first encounter of the Russians with that tribe. In the first half-

21.text: century, however, this was rather difficult, because of the absence of priests

22.text: or missionaries. Thus, Argentov mentions that in the chapel of the Kolyma,

23.text: in the absence of priests, the service was performed by laymen. Even later

24.text: laymen would perform baptism. Nil, Archbishop of Irkutsk, even as late as

25.text: 1848, ordered the priests to denounce and extirpate this evil.³

26.text: The first church in the Kolyma district was built in Nishne-Kolymsk

27.text: during the first years of the eighteenth century. In 1704 a communion-cloth

28.text: was sent from Tobolsk in western Siberia to Dog Fortress. In 1771 Sredne-

29.text: Kolymsk had also a church, that of the Intercession of the Holy Virgin, but

30.text: this church was a “black” one.⁴ In the same year Sredne-Kolymsk had only

31.text: three houses. About the same time Verkhne-Kolymsk had only a chapel

32.text: dedicated to St. Nicholas. The Anadyr Church, according to Argentov, was

33.text: built in 1743. The next year the first missionary, the monk Flavian, with

34.text: three assistants, was sent to this country; but all of them were murdered by
